blocks.p: **Disclaimer: This information is NOT meant to diagnose.  If you feel like you may be experiencing symptoms of bipolar disorder, consult with a mental health or medical professional.  We are speaking in generalities.  Your specific situation, diagnosis, treatment and medication are entirely between you and your provider.
MANIA & MAJOR DEPRESSIVE EPISODES
Fluctuation between extreme highs and lows
TOPIC: TYPES OF BIPOLAR DISORDER

ul: Bipolar I disorder is a manic-depressive disorder that can exist both with and without psychotic episodes
Bipolar II disorder consists of depressive and manic episodes which alternate and are typically less severe and do not inhibit function
Cyclothymic disorder is a cyclic disorder that causes brief episodes of hypomania and depression

blocks.p: A manic episode is a period of at least one week when a person is very high spirited or irritable in an extreme way most of the day for most days, has more energy than usual and experiences at least three of the following, showing a change in behavior:
Exaggerated self-esteem or grandiosity

ul: Sympathetic charge
Story follows state
Flight or fight energy?  Dunno.

blocks.p: Less need for sleep

ul: Sympathetically active
Can't fall asleep when in flight/fight

blocks.p: Talking more than usual, talking loudly and quickly

ul: Loss of vocal prosody when in sympathetic
Shorter breathing leads to faster rate of speaking

blocks.p: Easily distracted

ul: Sympathetically active due to neuroception of danger
Always scanning the environment

blocks.p: Doing many activities at once, scheduling more events in a day than can be accomplished

ul: Sympathetic energy with no place to direct it
Lack of mindfulness of the energy, not being in the moment
Not feeling the root of the energy, just acting
Probably a low tolerance to being in the moment

blocks.p: Increased risky behavior (e.g., reckless driving, spending sprees)

ul: No direction for the energy

blocks.p: Uncontrollable racing thoughts or quickly changing ideas or topics

ul: Anxious or aggressive thinking of the sympathetic state

blocks.p: A hypomanic episode is similar to a manic episode (above) but the symptoms are less severe and need only last four days in a row. Hypomanic symptoms do not lead to the major problems that mania often causes and the person is still able to function.
A major depressive episode is a period of two weeks in which a person has at least five of the following (including one of the first two):
Intense sadness or despair; feeling helpless, hopeless or worthless

ul: Shutdown
Empty, foggy, detached

blocks.p: Loss of interest in activities once enjoyed

ul: Anhedonia, the life force energy is gone
The sympathetic connection or motivation

blocks.p: Feeling worthless or guilty

ul: Very much the feelings of being in a shutdown as well

blocks.p: Sleep problems: sleeping too little or too much

ul: Too much is a shutdown thing
Too little might be due to some sympathetic energy returning
Or shutdown danger cues being too overwhelming?

blocks.p: Feeling restless or agitated (e.g., pacing or hand-wringing), or slowed speech or movements

ul: Sympathetic or shutdown
Undirected energy of sympathetic emerging
